file.readme:
ArduinoKernel -- a DOS-style shell for the Arduino UNO R4 WiFi.

Runs bare metal on the Renesas RA4M1 (Cortex-M4F, 48 MHz).
No RTOS, no allocator, no garbage collector. Static buffers only.

Type HELP for the command list.
file.config:
REM ArduinoKernel boot configuration
DEVICE=CONSOLE.SYS /BAUD:115200 /BITS:8N1
DEVICE=LEDMTX.SYS  /ROWS:8 /COLS:12
FILES=8
BUFFERS=2
file.autoexec:
@ECHO OFF
REM Runs automatically at boot. Edit it in kernel/i18n/*.json
REM or re-run it at any time with: RUN AUTOEXEC.BAT
VER
LED HEART
ECHO System ready.
file.hardware:
Arduino UNO R4 WiFi (ABX00087)

U1  Renesas R7FA4M1AB3CFM  Cortex-M4F 48 MHz, 256K flash, 32K SRAM
M1  ESP32-S3-MINI-1-N8     Xtensa LX7, 512K SRAM, 8M flash
U4  TXB0108DQSR            5V <-> 3V3 level translator
U2  NLASB3157DFT2G         USB D+ mux  (RA4M1 <-> ESP32-S3)
U6  NLASB3157DFT2G         USB D- mux

The ESP32-S3 reaches no header pin. All 14 digital, 6 analog,
I2C, SPI, UART, CAN and the 12x8 LED matrix belong to the RA4M1.

help.d.help:
Lists every command on this terminal, grouped by where its output
  actually appears -- some commands print here, some light the LED
  panel on the board, some talk to the second chip.

    HELP              the grouped list
    HELP <command>    everything about one command

  Commands are not case sensitive; HELP, help and Help all work.
help.d.echo:
Prints its argument on THIS terminal -- the window you are typing
  in. Nothing reaches the LED panel; TEXT and SCROLL do that.

    ECHO hello world      prints: hello world
    ECHO                  prints an empty line

  Chiefly useful inside batch files, to label what is happening as
  they run. See HELP RUN.
help.d.rpg:
THE SHADOW OF THE LOST ROAD -- a story game on THIS terminal.

  You wake at a river ford with no memory of arriving and a younger
  brother who was there long enough to get cold. He knows your name.
  He will not say it.

  THE HERO has twelve stats on a point buy: each starts at 3, you
  spend 90 points, 18 is the ceiling. That totals 126 -- an average of
  10.5, exactly where the D&D modifier crosses from negative to
  positive, so a flat spread is a competent unheroic person and an 18
  has to come out of somewhere else. Health and stamina follow Skyrim
  (a floor plus a per-point increment), carry weight follows Fallout
  (linear in Strength), and armour, perception, initiative and attack
  rolls come straight from D&D 5e.

  FOUR PEOPLE will travel with you and two will keep together on one
  road. Andrei is there from the first minute; the other three have to
  be asked, on J, and each wants proof rather than coin. Lenuta the
  hunter will not walk out with somebody who has not stood on the
  bridge. Costache has lost four sheep and says it was not wolves --
  bring him one. Damian wants you to have sworn something in front of
  the watch, which is the first thing in this game that reads the oath.

  A companion has four stats rather than twelve -- they are fought
  alongside, not played -- plus morale, which is mechanical: below 30
  they still fight what reaches them but will not walk into anything.

  You give one order, and it is the whole of your control over them.
  STAND WITH ME keeps them beside you, and since enemies go for whoever
  is nearest, a body beside you is a body between you and the next
  blow. TAKE THE FIGHT TO THEM closes with the nearest enemy. HOLD is
  for Lenuta, whose bow reaches six squares and who is a worse knife.
  Morale overrides all three: somebody shaken guards whatever you said.

  Damian does not fight well and is not there to. Once a fight, when
  you are below half, he mends instead of swinging.

  Once somebody trusts you -- morale 60 -- they ask to be taken
  somewhere. Take them and they are changed for good: a little tougher,
  a little better, and their morale stops falling below fifty.

  WAIT HERE leaves somebody exactly where you are standing, and they
  stay there until you walk back for them. Everything about them --
  morale, pack, the task they asked for -- is still theirs when you do.

  SEVEN STREETS run through Vadul Alb, and each has a name and a
  length. Ulita Stramba to the Old Tavern is four minutes; Ulita
  Fierarilor is ten; Drumul Vadului follows the water round and is
  twelve. The menu says which street you would take and how long it
  is, because a village is a handful of named roads and not a list of
  neighbours.

  THREE ROADS LEAVE IT. Drumul Padurii goes an hour and a quarter to
  the black forest, Drumul Holdelor fifty-five minutes to the cut
  fields, Drumul Podului nearly two hours to the stone bridge. Those
  are the ones with something on them, and the chance of meeting it
  goes up by a quarter after dark.

  A long road means when you set out matters. Leave for the bridge at
  five and you arrive in the dark whatever the light was when you
  started. Under the forest canopy only full day counts as light at
  all, so the wood wants a torch two hours before the village does.

  You cannot take a road out in the dark without a torch. It burns for
  the one trip. Lenuta the hunter warns you the first time you speak
  to her and also sells you the answer.

  IN THE FOREST you can work the wood for game -- a perception check
  on whichever of Vision, Hearing and Instinct is sharpest, ninety
  minutes, and a bad roll means it finds you first. IN THE FIELDS you
  can glean what the carts left: an apple is certain, grain is an
  Endurance roll. That is where hunger has an answer that is not coin.

  SIX WAYS TO PLAY, chosen once at the start and not changeable
  afterwards. What a difficulty moves here are rates the game already
  ran on -- how fast hunger climbs, how much of a blow lands, how busy
  the roads are, how much of you is left after losing -- and not enemy
  hit points, because a wolf with forty health is a longer fight and
  not a different one. Medium is the game exactly as it shipped in
  0.23.0 through 0.26.0, to the number.

  REALISTIC is not Very Hard plus a bit. It turns on two systems the
  other five do not have. Thirst runs faster than hunger and a dry
  mouth costs a square of movement and two off every attack; water is
  sold at the inn, the tavern, the Hearth and the bridge. Poison takes
  an ability score with it, so while it is in you every modifier on the
  sheet is one lower. Wolves and the Strigoi both carry it, and a salve
  draws half its healing out of it.

  TIME PASSES. A 24-hour clock, seven-day weeks, twelve months of
  thirty days. Hunger rises a point every forty minutes on Medium, for
  you and for him. The months carry their old Romanian folk names -- Gerar the
  frost, Cuptor the oven, Brumar the frost-bringer. They are names,
  and this shell does not translate names. The weekdays are ordinary
  words and do follow LANG.

  THE BAG holds twelve stacks, and three more slots are what you have
  in hand and on your back. Weight is in grams and the limit is
  Fallout's -- linear in Strength -- so over-laden costs you a square
  of movement in a fight. ENTER eats, drinks, wears, wields or takes
  off. G hands one across to Andrei and takes one back; he has four
  slots of his own and he eats out of them.

  THE VILLAGE REMEMBERS YOU, and forgets. Every conversation leaves two
  traces: they see your face every time and are told your name once, so
  a face goes in faster and fades faster. Deeds last most of a year and
  a bond -- a vow sworn in front of the watch, or agreeing to walk out
  of the village with somebody -- does not fade at all.

  The model is Ebbinghaus, who measured his own forgetting in 1885 and
  found retention falling exponentially with each recall flattening the
  curve. Two things follow, and both are felt. Massed repetition is
  worth almost nothing: talk to somebody four times in one afternoon
  and the fourth is free. Spacing is worth everything: come back the
  next morning and it counts in full.

  Presence is what decides how slowly they forget, which is the first
  thing that has ever read that stat. And the condition you turn up in
  sets how strongly a memory forms -- hungry, thirsty and poisoned each
  take a quarter off the impression you make, because you were not
  yourself. Eat before you ask a favour.

  What it buys is goodwill: up to fifteen percent off what they ask and
  on top of what they pay. A village that halved its prices for a
  regular would be an economy solved by talking to everybody twice.

  EIGHT of the fourteen villagers trade. Press T while talking to
  them. What they stock is what they would actually have: Dimitrie
  sells mail, Lenuta sells arrows, Grigore on the bridge sells what
  somebody who has walked two hours actually wants.

  BATTLE is on a 12x8 grid. Arrows move; moving into an enemy attacks
  with whatever is in your hand. F strikes at the weapon's reach, so a
  spear hits from two squares and a bow from six -- a bow spends an
  arrow to do it. d20 + attack bonus against armour class, then the
  weapon's damage die. A natural 20 always hits and a natural 1 always
  misses. Losing is not death: you wake at 1 health inside the gate,
  even if the road you lost on was two hours out.

  SEVEN THINGS will fight you. Five punish a different weakness --
  speed, numbers, armour, raw damage, cold. Ostas and Calaret are the
  exception and are meant to be: they are ranks, they are on the
  bridge road, and Kondos drills thirty-five houses that have never
  been attacked because of them.

  SAVING writes to the RA4M1's own data flash -- block 6, not the last
  block, because DF erases that one. The record carries a magic word,
  a format version and a CRC, and each catches a different failure.


  THE MAP, on M, is drawn to scale. Every place has a position in
  minutes of walking, solved so the straight line between two
  neighbours is the time their road charges. Arrows pan, +/- zoom.
  Zoom out far enough and the nine places of the village become one
  marker on three long roads, because at six columns across they are
  not nine places -- they are a blot. Names that would land on each
  other are dropped, nearest thing you care about first.
help.d.type:
Prints a file from drive A: on THIS terminal.

  A: is a read-only volume compiled into the board's flash. There is
  no disk, nothing can be written, and every board running this
  firmware version holds exactly the same files.

    TYPE HARDWARE.TXT
    TYPE README.TXT

  The name must match what DIR shows, extension included.
help.d.dir:
Lists drive A: on THIS terminal: name, extension, size, date.

  One volume, no subdirectories. The files live in flash and are
  fixed when the firmware is built, so they are identical on every
  board running this version.

  TYPE prints a file; RUN executes a batch file.
help.d.led:
Lights a fixed pattern on the LED MATRIX -- the 12x8 grid of red
  LEDs on the board itself. Nothing appears on this terminal beyond
  the confirmation line.

    LED ON       every LED lit        LED SMILE    a face
    LED OFF      every LED dark       LED HEART    a heart
    LED TEST     checkerboard

  Any scrolling text is stopped first: a still pattern and a moving
  marquee cannot share the panel. See HELP TEXT and HELP SCROLL.
help.d.text:
Holds a short word still on the LED MATRIX on the board.

  The panel is 12 pixels wide and the font is 5 wide with 1 of
  spacing, so about two characters fit at once. Anything longer is
  cut off -- use SCROLL for text that has to be read.

    TEXT OK
    TEXT HI

  Letters, digits and punctuation up to ASCII 0x5F; lower case is
  folded to upper. Nothing is printed on this terminal.
help.d.scroll:
Slides text across the LED MATRIX on the board.

    SCROLL <direction> <text>    direction: L R U D
    SCROLL <text>                same as L
    SCROLL OFF                   stop and blank the panel

    SCROLL L HELLO WORLD    leftwards, the usual choice
    SCROLL R ARDUINO        rightwards
    SCROLL U OK             upwards
    SCROLL D OK             downwards

  Up to 48 characters. The step interval comes from SPEED. Scrolling
  carries on while you type other commands -- it is not a mode, and
  the prompt stays usable throughout.
help.d.speed:
Milliseconds between animation steps on the LED MATRIX. Lower is
  faster. Affects SCROLL only; nothing on this terminal changes.

    minimum        10 ms     anything lower is raised to this
    maximum      2000 ms     anything higher is lowered to this
    default        90 ms

    SPEED          report the current value
    SPEED 40       quicker
    SPEED 250      slower

  SPEED on its own lasts until the next reboot. SETUP stores the
  value in the ESP32's memory, which survives a power cycle.
help.d.lang:
Sets the language of every message: this terminal, the boot
  screen, SETUP, and the help you are reading now. Saved at once, so
  it survives a reboot.

    LANG           report the current language
    LANG EN        English
    LANG RO        Romanian

  The LED panel uses a 5x7 ASCII font, so SCROLL renders Romanian
  without diacritics. That is a limit of the font, not of the
  translation.

  Both languages live in flash compressed: 92 KB of prose fits
  in 54 KB, by byte-pair encoding -- a code per common pair of
  characters, applied over and over -- and nothing is unpacked into a
  buffer: the words are spelled straight onto the screen as they are
  decoded. The longest page here is 8 KB and this chip has 32.
help.d.tft:
Drives an optional SPI TFT panel wired to the board's SPI header.
  None is fitted by default, and with no panel connected every form
  of the command reports that nothing answered.

    TFT ID              read the controller ID
    TFT ON              draw the boot banner on the panel
    TFT OFF             blank it
    TFT TEST            colour bars
    TFT TEXT <words>    one centred line

  TFT ID is the command that tells you whether the panel is really
  there: 0x009341 means an ILI9341 answered. Anything else means
  absent, miswired, or a different controller.
help.d.pins:
Shows every GPIO pin on the microcontroller: whether it belongs to
  GPIO or to a peripheral, its direction, and the level actually
  present on it at this moment.

    PINS               one snapshot
    PINS WATCH         keeps updating until you press a key
    PINS WATCH 3.2     the same, with port 3 pin 2 pulled up

  One character per pin:

    0  input, low            L  output, driving low
    1  input, high           H  output, driving high
    p  given to a peripheral  a  switched to analog

  WATCH identifies a header pin without trusting a table: ground the
  pin and watch which cell changes. Only changed cells are resent, so
  an update costs a few bytes instead of the ~700 the whole map takes.

  A floating input has no defined level, so add the pull-up form when
  you want a clean result: the named pin then rests at 1 and grounding
  it reads 0, unambiguously. P3.01 and P3.02 are the D0 and D1 header
  holes and are the easiest place to start, because where they go is
  known rather than guessed.

  ONE pin, and one you name. An earlier version pulled up everything
  that looked unclaimed and took the board off USB, needing a physical
  replug. "This firmware has not claimed it" is not "nothing is wired
  to it": the notes below list what this code configures and say
  nothing about what the board connects. Pins in use -- peripherals,
  outputs, the LED matrix -- are refused.

  Nothing else here writes. Reporting a pin cannot break anything;
  driving one that something else is already holding is two output
  stages fighting with nothing to limit the current.

  Matrix pins flicker while a pattern shows: the panel is
  charlieplexed and the scan interrupt redrives them thousands of
  times a second. That is the display working, not a fault.
help.d.theme:
Chooses how the full-screen views colour THIS TERMINAL: the boot
  screen, SETUP, and the games.

    PLAIN     your terminal's own background, colour used only for
              accents -- the [ OK ] tags, the selected row, sprites
    BIOS      bright white on blue, the way PC firmware looked
    MONO      positioning but no colour at all

  PLAIN is the default, and the reason is the window. On the SPI TFT
  the kernel owns every pixel of the panel, so a blue field fills it
  and looks exactly like firmware. A terminal window belongs to you:
  its size and its colours are yours, and an 80x25 blue field painted
  inside it is a rectangle floating in somebody else's theme, with a
  hard edge wherever the paint stopped.

  So the destination decides. The TFT keeps the firmware blue no
  matter what this is set to; only the terminal follows it.

  Saved at once, so it survives a reboot. SETUP has it too.
help.d.page:
How many rows of output before the shell stops and waits, so a long
  listing can be read without scrolling back for it.

    PAGE           report the current setting
    PAGE 24        pause every 24 rows -- the default
    PAGE 40        for a taller window
    PAGE OFF       never pause

  At the pause:

    SPACE          next screenful
    ENTER          one more line
    Q or ESC       stop, and abandon the rest of the output

  Saved, so it survives a reboot.

  This is what DOS did, and it is the right answer here for a reason:
  the alternative -- making the shell a full-screen program with a
  fixed prompt -- also stops the scrolling, but only by throwing the
  scrollback away. You could no longer look at something from five
  commands ago, because it would not exist. Paging keeps the history
  and removes the need to chase it.

  Full-screen views (SETUP, ESP, PINS WATCH, the games) never page:
  they already own the screen and never scroll at all.

  Paging is also suppressed inside batch files. AUTOEXEC.BAT runs
  before there is anybody at the keyboard, and a prompt there would
  stop the boot dead.
help.d.at:
Sends a command straight to the ESP32-S3 and prints whatever comes
  back, stopping as soon as it answers OK or ERROR.

  The command name is folded to upper case for you: the bridge only
  accepts it that way. Anything after an = is left alone, because that
  is data rather than syntax. A missing + is inserted, so AT GMR and
  AT+GMR are the same request.

  The ESP32-S3 is the SECOND chip on this board. It is not the one
  running this kernel; it holds the Wi-Fi radio and the settings
  store, and the two chips talk over an internal serial link. AT
  commands are that conversation, made visible.

    AT                  link check; answers OK
    AT+GMR              bridge firmware version
    AT+PREFSTAT         report the settings store
    AT+PREFGET=lang     read one saved setting
    AT+SOFTRESETWIFI    reset the radio

  Caution: this is a raw passthrough with no validation. A command
  the bridge does not expect can leave it unresponsive, and clearing
  that takes physically unplugging the USB cable -- the RESET button
  will not do it, because it does not power-cycle the ESP32.
help.d.esp:
A menu of the commands that have been sent to THIS bridge and seen
  to answer. Arrows select, Enter runs, ESC leaves. The reply appears
  in the pane below the list.

  This is the safe way to talk to the ESP32-S3, and the reason it
  exists is that AT is not. AT is a raw passthrough with no
  validation, and the bridge is the chip that presents USB: a command
  it does not expect can leave it unresponsive, and clearing that
  needs the cable physically unplugged. Typing command names by hand
  is the riskiest thing this shell offers.

  Here you cannot select something unproven, because unproven things
  are not in the list. Nothing is added to it on the strength of a
  guess.

  Currently: link check, firmware version, settings store, Wi-Fi
  scan, client socket, radio reset.

  AT remains for exploring; this is for using what exploring found.
help.d.debug:
Traces the serial link to the ESP32-S3 on THIS terminal: what was
  sent, how long the first byte took to come back, and any
  non-printable bytes shown as hex.

    DEBUG          report whether the trace is on
    DEBUG ON       start tracing
    DEBUG OFF      stop

  Useful when a command answers nothing and you want to know whether
  it was ignored or is simply slow. AT+WIFISCAN takes the better part
  of ten seconds, which is long enough to look like silence.

  Also turns PINS WATCH into an instrument: it then reports what each
  update costs on the wire against what a full repaint would, which is
  the entire claim behind the differential renderer.

  The ESP menu never prints trace output: it draws a full screen and a
  stray line would land in the middle of it.
help.d.run:
Executes a batch file from drive A:. A batch file is plain text,
  one command per line, run top to bottom exactly as if you had
  typed each line here yourself.

    RUN AUTOEXEC.BAT

  AUTOEXEC.BAT also runs on its own at every boot, between the
  banner and the first prompt -- that is where to put commands you
  want on every start.

  DIR lists what is on A:, and TYPE shows a file's contents before
  you run it. Batch files are built into the firmware and cannot be
  created at runtime.
help.d.df:
Erases, programs and reads back ONE block of the RA4M1's 8 KB data
  flash -- the last one, which holds nothing.

    DF                 size, block size, and a hex dump of the block
    DF ERASE           erase it, then confirm it reads back all FF
    DF WRITE <text>    erase, program the text, read it back and compare

  This is a diagnostic, not a filesystem. The driver is the first thing
  in this project that modifies non-volatile memory, and the way to
  earn trust in it is to write a pattern, read it back, then power
  cycle and look again. DF WRITE HELLO, then REBOOT, then DF.

  It cannot brick the board. The flash sequencer is put into one of
  two modes, and the mode decides which array it can reach; the driver
  only ever selects the data flash one, and the code flash values are
  absent from its source entirely. The worst case is losing 8 KB that
  nothing depends on -- LANG, THEME, SPEED and DEBUG live in the
  ESP32's memory, on the other chip.

  Flash can only clear bits, so DF WRITE erases first. Programming
  over existing data without erasing gives you the AND of the two,
  which is a confusing way to discover this.

  Rated for 100,000 erase cycles per block.
msg.nomodem: No modem link on this platform.
msg.nodf: No data flash on this platform.
msg.usagedf: Usage: DF | DF ERASE | DF WRITE <text>
df.notblank: Block is NOT erased -- the erase reported success but did nothing.
df.verified: Read back and matched. Reboot and run DF again to prove it persists.
df.mismatch: Read back did NOT match what was written.
df.howto: DF ERASE clears this block, DF WRITE <text> erases then programs it.

rpg.map.keys: arrows pan   +/- zoom   ENTER centre   Q back

rpg.swear.title: The Vow
rpg.vow.shield: I leave no one behind me.
rpg.vow.truth: I speak no lie, whatever it costs.
rpg.vow.hand: I take nothing that is not given.
rpg.oath.strained: Something in the words gives, and does not spring back.
rpg.oath.broken: The fence is down. You will not say the words tomorrow.
rpg.intro:
You woke face down in the mud of a river ford, with no memory of arriving and one boot missing. Your brother Andrei was sitting on the bank beside you, and he had been there long enough to be cold.

He knows your name. He knows the road you came down. He will not say either, and the way he will not say them is the frightening part.

The village is called Vadul Alb. Thirty-five houses, three places to eat and drink, two forges, and a walled yard where the captain drills whoever will come. Nobody here knows you. Several of them are being polite about it.
rpg.sheet.title: Character
rpg.name.title: Your name
rpg.name.ask:
The innkeeper is waiting with his ledger open. He has asked twice now, politely, and is beginning to suspect you do not know.

Whatever you tell him is what this village will call you.
rpg.name.label: Name:
rpg.name.keys: letters   BACKSPACE   ENTER accept   ESC cancel
rpg.p.square:
The square is packed earth with a well at one end and a stone the size of a cart at the other, which nobody can explain and everybody leans on.

Five ways out. The lanes run west into the houses, the big forge smokes to the east, and the north gate stands open onto the road.
rpg.p.lanes:
Thirty-five houses, close enough that an argument in one is a matter of public record in three. Ropes of onions, a goat on a chain, a boy who has decided to follow you.

The doors are shut but not barred. That is either trust or short memory.
rpg.p.stag:
The Stag is the good inn, which in Vadul Alb means the roof is whole and the beer is only mostly water. Nikos keeps a ledger nobody has ever seen him consult.

There are beds upstairs. Three coins, and he will not haggle.
rpg.p.old:
The Old Tavern is one room, one bench and a fire that draws badly. Despina serves without looking up.

The men at the bench stopped talking when you came in, which is how you know they were talking about you.
rpg.p.hearth:
The Hearth is not an inn. It is Iorgu's kitchen with the door taken off, and the whole village eats here when someone dies or marries.

Something with bay leaves in it has been going since yesterday.
rpg.p.forge.big:
The big forge. Dimitrie works iron for carts and ploughs and, when the captain insists, for other things.

A blade half-finished lies on the anvil under a cloth. He has not mentioned it and you have not asked.
rpg.p.forge.ford:
The ford forge is smaller and older, wedged between the water and the road, and Anghel mostly shoes horses.

He has been here longer than the big forge and does not discuss it.
rpg.p.yard:
A walled yard of trodden clay, straw men on posts, and a rack of practice blades with the edges taken off.

Captain Kondos drills anyone who turns up, in a village that has never once been attacked. He is not doing it for fun.
rpg.p.gate:
The north gate is two posts and a beam, and the road beyond it goes up into country that gets colder with every mile.

There is a reason the gate is watched at night and nobody has told you what it is.
rpg.say.elder:
"You came up out of the ford, and the ford runs south. So you came from the north, and there is nothing north of here but the pass."

She looks at you for a while.

"I am eighty-one. I have seen four people come down that road. You are the fourth."
rpg.say.child:
"Are you a soldier? Vasile says you stand like one. He says people stand like what they used to be even when they have forgotten it."

He is walking backwards so as not to stop looking at you.
rpg.say.healer:
"No fever, no bite, no crack in the skull. Whatever took your memory did not do it by hitting you, and that is the part I do not like."

She wipes her hands.

"Come back if you start dreaming in a language you do not speak."
rpg.say.priest:
"We buried a man from the pass in the spring. No name on him either."

"I am not saying that to frighten you. I am saying it because you will hear it from somebody less careful."
rpg.say.shepherd:
"Lost four sheep this month and not one of them to wolves. Wolves leave something."

"Do not tell Zoe I said that."
rpg.say.innkeep:
"Bed is three. Food is what Iorgu is making. If you have no coin you can have the bench by the fire and we will call it even, but do not make a habit of it."

He writes something in the ledger. It is a very short entry.
rpg.say.taverner:
"They will tell you the pass is closed for the snow. It is the fourth of the month and there is no snow."

She fills a cup you did not order and puts it down hard enough to end the conversation.
rpg.say.cook:
"Sit. Eat. You have the look of a man who has been walking since before he can remember, which in your case is a joke and I apologise."

It is the best thing you have eaten. You have nothing to compare it with.
rpg.say.hunter:
"I will not go past the second bridge after dark and neither will the dogs. The dogs decided first."

"If you are going up the road, go in the morning and come back before the light turns."
rpg.say.smith:
"Iron is iron. You bring me metal, I will make it into whatever you need, and I will charge you for it because I have a family."

He does not look at the cloth on the anvil while he says this.
rpg.say.farrier:
"Dimitrie is the better smith and he will tell you so himself. I am the older one."

"There was a forge here before there was a village. Ask the priest what the foundations are."
rpg.say.captain:
"Thirty-five houses and no wall worth the name. I drill them anyway because the alternative is finding out in one night what I could have taught them in a year."

He looks you over the way you look over a tool.

"You know how to stand. Stay. Take a vow with the rest of them, if you have the stomach for one -- I would rather know now."
rpg.say.merchant: "North? Nobody goes north. I come the long way round through three valleys and I still make money, which should tell you what the short way is worth."
rpg.swear.body:
Kondos does not make a ceremony of it. The watch take one vow each, and only one, and they say it where the others can hear.

It is not a promise about what you will do. It is a fence around what you will not.

Choose the fence you can hold.
rpg.rest.title: The Stag
rpg.rested: You sleep until the shutters go grey, and wake whole. Andrei was up before you and has not said how long he was awake.
rpg.no.coin: Nikos looks at your empty hand, then at the ledger. Not tonight.
rpg.battle.keys: arrows move or strike   F at reach   ENTER wait   ESC flee
rpg.won.title: Victory
rpg.lost.title: Down
rpg.lost: You come round face down again, which is becoming a habit. Somebody has dragged you back inside the gate and left you your boots.
rpg.fled.title: Away
rpg.fled: You break off and run, and nothing follows you far.
rpg.level.title: Stronger
rpg.level: Level {}. Whatever you used to be, some of it is coming back.
rpg.save.title: Save
rpg.saved: Written to the data flash. It will survive a power cut.
rpg.save.fail: The save failed at step {}. Nothing was written.
rpg.no.store: No data flash on this platform -- saving is unavailable.
rpg.who.title: Who you are
rpg.who.body:
Andrei answers most of it before you can. He is used to speaking for you, which is its own piece of information.

The rest you find out by looking down.
rpg.buy.title: What you are made of
rpg.buy.hint: Every stat starts at 3. Ninety points to spend, eighteen is the ceiling, and nothing comes free.
rpg.buy.keys: up/down pick   left/right spend   ENTER accept   ESC back
rpg.comp.brother: Younger than you by four years, and the only person in the world who knows what that means.
rpg.say.brother: "You are doing the thing again. Where you look at me like you are checking I am still the same one."
rpg.say.brother.he:
"You are doing the thing again, brother. Where you look at me like you are checking I am still the same one."

He is trying to make it a joke. It is not landing for either of you.
rpg.say.brother.she:
"You are doing the thing again, sister. Where you look at me like you are checking I am still the same one."

She is not the word he wanted. He tried three before he got there, and he has never had to try before.
rpg.say.hungry:
"I am not complaining. I am reporting."

He has been walking behind you for an hour so you cannot see his face while he says it.
rpg.say.shaken:
"I will come. I will just not be in front."

He is holding the practice blade the way you hold something you have decided not to drop, which is not the same as holding a weapon.
rpg.road.title: The Road Out
rpg.too.dark:
Lenuta was plain about it: not past the second bridge after dark, and the dogs decided before she did.

Beyond the last house the road is a darker line in a dark field, and you have nothing to carry in front of you. You can go in the morning.
rpg.bag.title: Bag
rpg.bag.keys: arrows pick   ENTER use   G give   X drop   Q back
rpg.bag.full: There is no room for it.
rpg.shop.keys: arrows pick   ENTER trade   Q back
rpg.trade.hint: -- T to trade, any other key to go --
rpg.loot.title: What is left
rpg.loot: You go through what is left on the ground. Worth keeping: {}.
rpg.no.arrows: reaches back and finds the quiver empty
rpg.torch.lit: You light a torch before the last house. It will last the road and not much further, and whoever is watching the dark can see exactly where you are.
rpg.p.forest:
Under the trees the light gives out two hours before it does anywhere else, and the noise of the village stops as though a door had shut behind you.

Something has been through here ahead of you. The tracks are not deer and they are not going anywhere in particular, which is worse.
rpg.p.fields:
Corn stubble to the treeline, and rye beyond that, all of it cut three weeks ago and picked over twice since. What is left is what the carts could not be bothered with.

Costache has the sheep up on the headland where he can count them. He counts them a great deal now.
rpg.p.bridge:
Three stone arches over water the colour of tea, and older than anything in Vadul Alb by four hundred years. Nobody knows who built it. The priest has a view and does not share it.

Everything that comes to the village comes over this. So does everything else.
rpg.say.watch:
"Two hours from the village and I am the whole garrison. Kondos sends me bread on Tuesdays and I send him back what I have counted."

He does not look at you while he talks. He watches the far end of the bridge, the way a man does when he has learned to.

"Nine carts and two companies since Gustar. The carts went south and came back. The companies went south and did not."
rpg.hunt.title: The Wood
rpg.hunt.good: You get downwind of it and wait, and it walks into you rather than the other way round. {} to carry home.
rpg.hunt.poor: Two hours of standing still in the cold, and the wood keeps what it has. Andrei has the sense not to say anything.
rpg.hunt.found: You find it by walking into it. It has been watching you work since the treeline and it is not frightened, which tells you what kind of winter it has had.
rpg.glean.title: The Fields
rpg.glean.some: An afternoon bent double for a handful of windfalls. It is food, and nobody grudges you it, and it is not much.
rpg.glean.good: The carts missed a corner where the rye went down in the rain. You come out of it with more than you went in for.
rpg.no.light: Not without light enough to see by. Come back when the sun is up.
rpg.ambush.title: On the Road
rpg.ambush: It comes off the bank on your left, and it has picked the spot -- there is no way past and the only way back is the way you came.
rpg.ask.title: A Word
rpg.party.full: Two is as many as will keep together on a road. Somebody would have to wait.
rpg.join.hint: -- J to ask them along, any other key to go --
rpg.both.hint: -- T to trade, J to ask them along, any other key to go --
rpg.task.title: Kept
rpg.join.brother: He does not answer. He has been following you since the ford and does not see what there is to agree to.
rpg.ask.brother:
"I want to see the bridge."

He says it to the fire, not to you.

"Everyone here talks about what comes down that road like it is weather. I want to stand on it once and see that it is a road."
rpg.thanks.brother:
He stood on the middle arch for a long time and did not say anything, and then he said it was smaller than he thought.

He has walked in front of you twice since. He did not used to do that.
rpg.comp.hunter: Forty years of a wood that has started keeping things from her. She carries a bow and the only opinion in the village that is based on having gone and looked.
rpg.say.k.hunter: "Keep me back and keep me pointed. I am no good to you in a crowd and I am very good to you at forty paces."
rpg.refuse.hunter:
"I said go in the morning and come back before the light turns. You have not been past the second bridge and I am not walking out there with somebody who has not."

She goes back to the string she is waxing.

"Go and stand on that bridge. Then ask me again."
rpg.join.hunter:
"You went up and you came back." She looks at you for a while longer than is comfortable. "That is two more than most."

She takes the bow off the wall without being asked twice.
rpg.ask.hunter:
"There is a place in the wood the dogs will not cross. Not will not go past -- will not cross, like a line somebody drew."

"I have not been able to make myself go alone. I am telling you that so you know what you are agreeing to."
rpg.thanks.hunter:
She stood on the line and nothing happened, and that seemed to be worse for her than if something had.

"Right," she said, eventually. "Right."

She has not mentioned it since and she has not left your side either.
rpg.comp.shepherd: A slow man with a heavy stick who has been counting the same flock for twenty years and can tell you which one is missing without looking twice.
rpg.say.k.shepherd: "I will stand in front. I am wider than you and I have been bitten before."
rpg.refuse.shepherd:
"Four sheep and not one of them to wolves. Wolves leave something -- a leg, a head, wool in the thorns. There was nothing."

"Bring me a wolf and I will believe I was wrong about it. Until then I am not leaving the flock to go and be wrong somewhere else."
rpg.join.shepherd:
He turns the wolf over with his boot for a long time.

"Then it was wolves after all," he says, and does not sound relieved. "I have been telling everyone it was not."

He whistles the dog up to the flock and picks up his stick.
rpg.ask.shepherd:
"If they came south, they came over that bridge. There is no other way down and I have walked every other way."

"I want to see the stone. That is all. I want to see whether anything crossed it."
rpg.thanks.shepherd:
He went along the parapet on his hands and knees looking at the moss, which took an hour, and at the end of it he said: "Something heavy. Shod. Going south."

He has not said another word about the sheep.
rpg.comp.priest: He buried a man from the pass in the spring with no name on him, and he has not been the same about the road since. He does not fight well. That is not what he is for.
rpg.say.k.priest: "Stay where I can reach you. That is all I ask and it is not a small ask."
rpg.refuse.priest:
"I have buried people who went up that road for their own reasons and I do not intend to bury one more."

"Swear something. Anything, to Kondos, in front of the watch. I do not care which. I want to know there is a thing you will not do, and I want somebody else to have heard you say it."
rpg.join.priest:
"Good." He does not ask which vow you took. "A man who has drawn a line will walk in a straight one."

He brings a satchel that clinks and a stick that is not a weapon.
rpg.ask.priest:
"The grave I dug in the spring is not where I told the village it is. It is in the wood, and it is not the only one there."

"Come out with me and stand where I can see you while I look at them again."
rpg.thanks.priest:
There were three. He knelt at each one for the same length of time and did not explain the arithmetic of that.

"Now you know as much as I do," he said on the way back. "I have wanted that for a month."
rpg.company.title: Company
rpg.company.body: Two will keep together on a road. Anybody else waits where you left them, and waits there until you go back.
rpg.diff.title: How hard
rpg.diff.body: This is the one choice here you cannot change afterwards. Everything else about the character is yours to spend; this is the world you spend it in.
rpg.diff.veryeasy.about:
Hunger takes an hour and a half a point. Blows land at half. The road is half as busy, and losing a fight costs you nothing but the time.

For the village and the people, and not the arithmetic.
rpg.diff.easy.about:
Hunger every seventy minutes, three quarters of every blow, and you wake at better than half after a beating.

Everything works; nothing much punishes you.
rpg.diff.medium.about:
Hunger every forty minutes, blows in full, the roads as dangerous as they were written. You wake at a quarter.

This is the game as it has always been. If you do not want a difficulty setting, this is the one you already had.
rpg.diff.hard.about:
Hunger every half hour and a quarter more damage than the dice say. The roads are busier and you wake at a tenth, which for most characters is one or two.

A salve stops being a luxury.
rpg.diff.veryhard.about:
Hunger every twenty-four minutes, half again on every blow against you, and losing leaves you exactly one health wherever the gate is.

What you carry starts deciding what you can attempt.
rpg.diff.realistic.about:
Everything Very Hard does, and two things it does not.

THIRST runs faster than hunger -- a point every twenty minutes -- and a dry mouth costs a square of movement and two off every attack. Water is sold at the inn, the tavern, the Hearth and the bridge, and weighs seven hundred grams a skin.

POISON takes an ability score with it. Wolves and the Strigoi both carry it, and while it is in you every modifier on the sheet is one lower.
rpg.poisoned: is bitten and it does not stop bleeding
rpg.know.name: your face and your name
help.dlc: Story loaded from the PC over the wire
help.d.dlc:
DLC                  what is loaded
  DLC LOAD             receive a pack over XMODEM-CRC
  DLC PLAY             read it
  DLC ERASE            forget it

  A pack is a chapter: scenes, prose, and choices that branch. It lives
  in the bottom six kilobytes of the data flash -- not block 6, which is
  the RPG's save, and not block 7, which DF erases.

  DLC LOAD sends 'C' once a second for ten seconds and then gives up.
  Any XMODEM-capable terminal can feed it. The tool that ships with this
  project is one command from the other end:

    akterm --send story.dlc

  which compiles the readable source, opens the port, types DLC LOAD for
  you and sends the result.

  XMODEM because a story arriving over a UART needs exactly what it has:
  a sequence number so a dropped block is noticed, a CRC so a flipped bit
  is noticed, and a retry so either can be fixed without starting again.
dlc.empty: No pack loaded. DLC LOAD to receive one.
dlc.no.store: No data flash on this platform.
dlc.erase: The erase failed. Nothing was written.
dlc.write: A block would not program. The pack is incomplete.
dlc.timeout: Nothing arrived. Start the sender within ten seconds.
dlc.too.big: Too big. Six kilobytes is the whole of the space.
dlc.not.a.pack: That transferred, but it is not a pack -- bad magic, version or CRC.
